title: Preserve astronomical coordinate provenance
prompt: An astronomical image has a WCS header with unknown pixel-origin convention. A catalog has several nearby candidates with different observation epochs. Can you report a unique counterpart from the nearest coordinate alone? Explain what must be checked. Do not edit files.
rubric: The response checks the WCS pixel-origin convention rather than assuming it.
It reports matching ambiguity and accounts for observation epochs and possible motion.
It does not claim the nearest candidate is automatically a unique physical counterpart.
acceptance: The response preserves coordinate and epoch provenance and does not assert an unsupported unique match.
